target_audience: Readers of geopolitical thrillers, military fiction, and techno-thrillers
gist: A geopolitical thriller about a modern war erupting over control of the Strait of Hormuz, tracing the choices of sailors, pilots, civilians, and leaders as the global economy teeters on the edge of collapse.
book_summary: A mysterious explosion sinks a Panama-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, blocking the world's most important energy chokepoint. Within hours, oil prices spike, markets panic, and old alliances strain. As naval forces converge, a cyber weapon of unknown origin turns the conflict into a war fought as much in silicon as in steel. The novel follows an American destroyer executive officer, an Iranian naval captain, a downed fighter pilot, a SEAL rescue team, and civilians on both shores as each tries to survive choices made by leaders they will never meet.

chapters.name: Introduction
chapters.chapter_summary: A frame opening over the Strait of Hormuz, establishing the chokepoint as the world's narrow gate and hinting at the war to come.
A tanker explodes in the Strait of Hormuz; Commander Lin and Captain Sharifi converge on the disaster as minor skirmishes begin.
Oil prices spike; governments scramble; a cyberattack blacks out port infrastructure across the UAE.
Iran deploys mines, speedboat swarms, and coastal anti-ship missiles; the USS Truxtun defends minesweepers under fire.
Amir discovers his own code may have triggered the tanker incident; cyber warfare cripples power grids and military networks.
Iran declares the strait closed to all traffic; civilian tankers are trapped, and a boarding action puts The Orion Pride in danger.
Operation 'Open Gate' begins; Morales leads SEAD missions until his wingman is shot down.
Master Chief Miller's team races to rescue the downed pilot before Iranian security forces close in.

chapters.chapter_title: The Human Cost on the Home Front
chapters.chapter_summary: Zahra evacuates a hospital under coastal strikes; global fuel riots and supply shortages spread.

chapters.chapter_title: The Decisive Battle of the Chokepoint
chapters.chapter_summary: The coalition clears the strait in a devastating engagement; Lin and Sharifi match wits across radar screens.
A fragile ceasefire opens the strait to limping traffic; survivors face a changed world order.

chapters.name: Conclusion
chapters.chapter_summary: A closing reflection on the strait as the world's narrow gate, asking whether a broken world can be reopened without new wounds.

all_characters.identity: Executive Officer of the USS Truxtun
all_characters.psychological_depth: Calm under pressure, responsible for holding the line when the strait becomes a battlefield.

all_characters.identity: Aging, pragmatic IRGCN officer on Qeshm Island
all_characters.psychological_depth: Understands the cost of escalation better than his superiors.
Her models predict catastrophic global recession if the strait stays closed.
Balances military deterrence with the last off-ramps of diplomacy.
Flies SEAD missions over the Iranian coast.
Inserted behind enemy lines to rescue Morales.
Realizes the algorithm he helped write is spinning out of control.
Works double shifts as civilian infrastructure collapses.

all_characters.identity: Master of the trapped supertanker Orion Pride
all_characters.psychological_depth: Manages panicking crew and dwindling supplies.

history: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most important energy chokepoint, through which a fifth of global oil passes. The novel imagines a near-future conflict over its control, fought as much in silicon (cyber warfare) as in steel (naval and air power).
